validation_source_categories: DRC Ministry of Health official bulletins
peer-reviewed epidemiological studies (Lancet, NEJM, Eurosurveillance, PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases)
disease_intelligence.suggested_geographic_granularity: ["national (DRC)", "provincial (e.g., South Kivu, North Kivu, Equateur, Sankuru, Maniema, Kinshasa)", "health zone (zone de santé)", "health area (aire de santé)"]
disease_intelligence.suggested_time_granularity: ["weekly (epidemiological week / semaine épidémiologique)", "monthly cumulative", "daily if available from sitreps"]
count_semantics_notes: DRC surveillance distinguishes: cas suspects (suspected), cas probables (probable), cas confirmés (confirmed by PCR/lab) — record each separately
Cumulative case counts are frequently reported; always note whether figure is cumulative-to-date or incident (new cases in period)
CFR (case fatality rate) in DRC clade I outbreaks is historically higher (~3–10%) than global clade IIb — do not apply global CFR benchmarks
Deaths may be underreported relative to cases due to community-level mortality not captured in facility-based surveillance
Hospitalization data is sparse in DRC context; capture when available but expect gaps
Epidemiological week (EW/SE) numbering should be mapped to calendar dates for the August 2024 window (EW31–EW35 approximately)
Some reports aggregate multiple provinces; disaggregate to province level where possible
disambiguation_risks: 'Mpox' vs. 'Smallpox' (variole) — ensure correct disease mapping
Clade I vs. Clade II vs. Clade Ib — DRC 2024 outbreak is predominantly clade I and emerging clade Ib; do not conflate with global clade IIb outbreak
'Monkeypox' legacy term still used in older documents and some French-language sources ('variole du singe') — treat as equivalent
Case classification ambiguity: DRC surveillance often reports 'cas suspects' as the primary count; confirmed PCR cases are a subset — do not sum across categories
Cumulative vs. incident (new) case counts — distinguish clearly; many sitreps report cumulative totals
Health zone vs. province — subnational granularity varies by source; record at finest available level
Pediatric mpox in DRC is disproportionately high — age-stratified data may be available and should be captured separately if present
PHEIC declaration (August 2024) may cause surge in reporting and retrospective revisions — flag data vintage carefully
exclusion_terms: mpox historical pre-2024 unless explicitly comparative
chickenpox (varicelle) — distinct disease, do not conflate

collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for Mpox (Monkeypox) from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Mpox (Monkeypox).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

count_semantics_notes: DRC surveillance distinguishes: cas suspects (suspected), cas probables (probable), cas confirmés (confirmed by PCR/lab) — record each separately
Cumulative case counts are frequently reported; always note whether figure is cumulative-to-date or incident (new cases in period)
CFR (case fatality rate) in DRC clade I outbreaks is historically higher (~3–10%) than global clade IIb — do not apply global CFR benchmarks
Deaths may be underreported relative to cases due to community-level mortality not captured in facility-based surveillance
Hospitalization data is sparse in DRC context; capture when available but expect gaps
Epidemiological week (EW/SE) numbering should be mapped to calendar dates for the August 2024 window (EW31–EW35 approximately)
Some reports aggregate multiple provinces; disaggregate to province level where possible
disambiguation_risks: 'Mpox' vs. 'Smallpox' (variole) — ensure correct disease mapping
Clade I vs. Clade II vs. Clade Ib — DRC 2024 outbreak is predominantly clade I and emerging clade Ib; do not conflate with global clade IIb outbreak
'Monkeypox' legacy term still used in older documents and some French-language sources ('variole du singe') — treat as equivalent
Case classification ambiguity: DRC surveillance often reports 'cas suspects' as the primary count; confirmed PCR cases are a subset — do not sum across categories
Cumulative vs. incident (new) case counts — distinguish clearly; many sitreps report cumulative totals
Health zone vs. province — subnational granularity varies by source; record at finest available level
Pediatric mpox in DRC is disproportionately high — age-stratified data may be available and should be captured separately if present
PHEIC declaration (August 2024) may cause surge in reporting and retrospective revisions — flag data vintage carefully

DATA COMPLETENESS: DRC surveillance infrastructure is resource-constrained; significant underreporting is expected, especially at health-zone and community levels
LANGUAGE: Primary official DRC sources are in French — query terms and source reading must accommodate French-language content ('cas', 'décès', 'flambée', 'bulletin épidémiologique', etc.)
TEMPORAL OVERLAP: August 2024 data may appear in reports dated September or October 2024 (retrospective sitreps) — do not restrict source search strictly to August publication dates

EXTRACTION MODEL WARNING (from task_input_warnings): extraction_record_model_still_hantavirus_named — verify that the extraction schema in use has been updated to Mpox-appropriate field names before ingestion; do not allow Hantavirus-specific fields to contaminate Mpox records

SOURCE DISCOVERY WARNING (from task_input_warnings): source_discovery_not_yet_disease_generic — source discovery pipeline may not yet be fully generalized; manually verify that Mpox-specific source categories (WHO DON, Africa CDC, INRB, DRC MoH) are included in the discovery scope
DOUBLE-COUNTING RISK: WHO, Africa CDC, and DRC MoH may report the same underlying data — cross-reference source chains and avoid double-counting when aggregating
SUBNATIONAL GRANULARITY: Prioritize province-level and health-zone-level data; national aggregates alone are insufficient for this collection task
EVIDENCE QUOTE REQUIREMENT: Every extracted record must include a verbatim evidence_quote from the source document supporting the numeric values recorded

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), WHO AFRO situation reports, and Africa CDC bulletins reporting Mpox cases and deaths in DRC for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON and Africa CDC are the highest-priority primary reporting channels for DRC Mpox during the August 2024 outbreak escalation period. These sources contain extractable confirmed, probable, suspected case counts and deaths at national and subnational level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique) and INRB epidemiological bulletins (bulletins épidémiologiques) for Mpox in DRC covering August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The DRC MoH and INRB are the national authoritative sources for subnational (province and health zone) Mpox surveillance data. French-language bulletins are the primary format and are essential for subnational_location and locality field extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Mpox situation reports and multi-country updates covering DRC for the period 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO global Mpox sitreps published in August 2024 aggregate DRC-specific data and may include subnational breakdowns, clade I/Ib distinctions, and weekly case/death counts extractable for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (Global.health, Our World in Data, ProMED) that aggregate DRC Mpox case and death counts for August 2024 for cross-validation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be held back and used to validate extracted records from primary collection sources without leakage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ECDC rapid risk assessments or technical reports covering DRC Mpox clade I/Ib for August 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ECDC published technical assessments on DRC Mpox clade Ib in mid-2024 that include epidemiological summaries usable for validation of case and death counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and preprints describing DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology, case definitions, and surveillance methodology for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources clarify case definitions (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), clade classification, and count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly) needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify news and situation report sources (Reuters, AP, Reliefweb, OCHA) covering DRC Mpox outbreak in August 2024 for early signal detection and subnational location corroboration.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and humanitarian situation reports may contain early outbreak signals, subnational location names, and corroborating counts that support collection and help identify gaps in official reporting.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident), unclear reporting periods, or mixed clade data for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: DRC Mpox reporting in August 2024 involved both clade I and clade Ib, cumulative and weekly counts, and national vs. subnational aggregations. Sources that do not clearly distinguish these dimensions require human adjudication.

These sources publish weekly and monthly epidemiological bulletins with subnational (province, health zone) case and death breakdowns, confirmed/probable/suspected case classifications, and clade I/Ib distinctions directly relevant to the August 2024...[truncated]

WHO global Mpox situation reports, ECDC rapid risk assessments, OCHA humanitarian situation reports, and Reliefweb updates provide independently compiled DRC Mpox data for August 2024. Essential for interpreting count semantics and normalizing confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.

Structured public-health databases including Global.health line lists, Our World in Data Mpox tracker, WHO Mpox data repository, and ProMED archive provide machine-readable or structured DRC Mpox counts for August 2024. These are held back for validation to cross-check extracted records from primary collection sources.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC), humanitarian portals (Reliefweb, OCHA), and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Health Policy Watch) published DRC Mpox outbreak coverage in August 2024 coinciding with the WHO PHEIC declaration. These sources provide early outbreak signals, subnational location corroboration, and may cite official figures directly quotable as evidence.

count_semantics_notes: DRC surveillance distinguishes: cas suspects (suspected), cas probables (probable), cas confirmés (confirmed by PCR/lab) — record each separately
Cumulative case counts are frequently reported; always note whether figure is cumulative-to-date or incident (new cases in period)
CFR (case fatality rate) in DRC clade I outbreaks is historically higher (~3–10%) than global clade IIb — do not apply global CFR benchmarks
Deaths may be underreported relative to cases due to community-level mortality not captured in facility-based surveillance
Hospitalization data is sparse in DRC context; capture when available but expect gaps
Epidemiological week (EW/SE) numbering should be mapped to calendar dates for the August 2024 window (EW31–EW35 approximately)
Some reports aggregate multiple provinces; disaggregate to province level where possible
disambiguation_risks: 'Mpox' vs. 'Smallpox' (variole) — ensure correct disease mapping
Clade I vs. Clade II vs. Clade Ib — DRC 2024 outbreak is predominantly clade I and emerging clade Ib; do not conflate with global clade IIb outbreak
'Monkeypox' legacy term still used in older documents and some French-language sources ('variole du singe') — treat as equivalent
Case classification ambiguity: DRC surveillance often reports 'cas suspects' as the primary count; confirmed PCR cases are a subset — do not sum across categories
Cumulative vs. incident (new) case counts — distinguish clearly; many sitreps report cumulative totals
Health zone vs. province — subnational granularity varies by source; record at finest available level
Pediatric mpox in DRC is disproportionately high — age-stratified data may be available and should be captured separately if present
PHEIC declaration (August 2024) may cause surge in reporting and retrospective revisions — flag data vintage carefully

These sources publish weekly and monthly epidemiological bulletins with subnational (province, health zone) case and death breakdowns, confirmed/probable/suspected case classifications, and clade I/Ib distinctions directly relevant to the August 2024...[truncated]

WHO global Mpox situation reports, ECDC rapid risk assessments, OCHA humanitarian situation reports, and Reliefweb updates provide independently compiled DRC Mpox data for August 2024. These serve as validation sources because they aggregate data from official DRC sources but are published independently, enabling cross-check of case and death counts.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints (PubMed, medRxiv, Lancet, NEJM, Eurosurveillance) on DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology published in 2024 provide case definitions, surveillance methodology context, and may contain extractable case/death data for the August 2024 period. Essential for interpreting count semantics and normalizing confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.

Structured public-health databases including Global.health line lists, Our World in Data Mpox tracker, WHO Mpox data repository, and ProMED archive provide machine-readable or structured DRC Mpox counts for August 2024. These are held back for validation to cross-check extracted records from primary collection sources.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC), humanitarian portals (Reliefweb, OCHA), and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Health Policy Watch) published DRC Mpox outbreak coverage in August 2024 coinciding with the WHO PHEIC declaration. These sources provide early outbreak signals, subnational location corroboration, and may cite official figures directly quotable as evidence.

Health zone vs. province — subnational granularity varies by source; record at finest available level

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), WHO AFRO situation reports, and Africa CDC bulletins reporting Mpox cases and deaths in DRC for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON and Africa CDC are the highest-priority primary reporting channels for DRC Mpox during the August 2024 outbreak escalation period. These sources contain extractable confirmed, probable, suspected case counts and deaths at national and subnational level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique) and INRB epidemiological bulletins (bulletins épidémiologiques) for Mpox in DRC covering August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The DRC MoH and INRB are the national authoritative sources for subnational (province and health zone) Mpox surveillance data. French-language bulletins are the primary format and are essential for subnational_location and locality field extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Mpox situation reports and multi-country updates covering DRC for the period 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO global Mpox sitreps published in August 2024 aggregate DRC-specific data and may include subnational breakdowns, clade I/Ib distinctions, and weekly case/death counts extractable for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (Global.health, Our World in Data, ProMED) that aggregate DRC Mpox case and death counts for August 2024 for cross-validation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be held back and used to validate extracted records from primary collection sources without leakage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ECDC rapid risk assessments or technical reports covering DRC Mpox clade I/Ib for August 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ECDC published technical assessments on DRC Mpox clade Ib in mid-2024 that include epidemiological summaries usable for validation of case and death counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and preprints describing DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology, case definitions, and surveillance methodology for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources clarify case definitions (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), clade classification, and count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly) needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify news and situation report sources (Reuters, AP, Reliefweb, OCHA) covering DRC Mpox outbreak in August 2024 for early signal detection and subnational location corroboration.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and humanitarian situation reports may contain early outbreak signals, subnational location names, and corroborating counts that support collection and help identify gaps in official reporting.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident), unclear reporting periods, or mixed clade data for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: DRC Mpox reporting in August 2024 involved both clade I and clade Ib, cumulative and weekly counts, and national vs. subnational aggregations. Sources that do not clearly distinguish these dimensions require human adjudication.

These sources publish weekly and monthly epidemiological bulletins with subnational (province, health zone) case and death breakdowns, confirmed/probable/suspected case classifications, and clade I/Ib distinctions directly relevant to the August 2024...[truncated]

WHO global Mpox situation reports, ECDC rapid risk assessments, OCHA humanitarian situation reports, and Reliefweb updates provide independently compiled DRC Mpox data for August 2024. These serve as validation sources because they aggregate data from official DRC sources but are published independently, enabling cross-check of case and death counts.

Essential for interpreting count semantics and normalizing confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.

Structured public-health databases including Global.health line lists, Our World in Data Mpox tracker, WHO Mpox data repository, and ProMED archive provide machine-readable or structured DRC Mpox counts for August 2024. These are held back for validation to cross-check extracted records from primary collection sources.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC), humanitarian portals (Reliefweb, OCHA), and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Health Policy Watch) published DRC Mpox outbreak coverage in August 2024 coinciding with the WHO PHEIC declaration. These sources provide early outbreak signals, subnational location corroboration, and may cite official figures directly quotable as evidence.

count_semantics_notes: DRC surveillance distinguishes: cas suspects (suspected), cas probables (probable), cas confirmés (confirmed by PCR/lab) — record each separately
Cumulative case counts are frequently reported; always note whether figure is cumulative-to-date or incident (new cases in period)
CFR (case fatality rate) in DRC clade I outbreaks is historically higher (~3–10%) than global clade IIb — do not apply global CFR benchmarks
Deaths may be underreported relative to cases due to community-level mortality not captured in facility-based surveillance
Hospitalization data is sparse in DRC context; capture when available but expect gaps
Epidemiological week (EW/SE) numbering should be mapped to calendar dates for the August 2024 window (EW31–EW35 approximately)
Some reports aggregate multiple provinces; disaggregate to province level where possible
disambiguation_risks: 'Mpox' vs. 'Smallpox' (variole) — ensure correct disease mapping
Clade I vs. Clade II vs. Clade Ib — DRC 2024 outbreak is predominantly clade I and emerging clade Ib; do not conflate with global clade IIb outbreak
'Monkeypox' legacy term still used in older documents and some French-language sources ('variole du singe') — treat as equivalent
Case classification ambiguity: DRC surveillance often reports 'cas suspects' as the primary count; confirmed PCR cases are a subset — do not sum across categories
Cumulative vs. incident (new) case counts — distinguish clearly; many sitreps report cumulative totals
Health zone vs. province — subnational granularity varies by source; record at finest available level
Pediatric mpox in DRC is disproportionately high — age-stratified data may be available and should be captured separately if present
PHEIC declaration (August 2024) may cause surge in reporting and retrospective revisions — flag data vintage carefully
exclusion_terms: mpox historical pre-2024 unless explicitly comparative
chickenpox (varicelle) — distinct disease, do not conflate
warnings: PHEIC CONTEXT: WHO declared mpox a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on 14 August 2024, driven substantially by the DRC clade Ib outbreak — expect elevated reporting volume, potential data revisions, and multiple overlapping sitreps during this window

CLADE SPECIFICITY: DRC August 2024 data involves both endemic clade I and the newly characterized clade Ib (associated with sexual transmission networks in eastern DRC, particularly South Kivu) — distinguish clade when reported
DATA COMPLETENESS: DRC surveillance infrastructure is resource-constrained; significant underreporting is expected, especially at health-zone and community levels
LANGUAGE: Primary official DRC sources are in French — query terms and source reading must accommodate French-language content ('cas', 'décès', 'flambée', 'bulletin épidémiologique', etc.)
TEMPORAL OVERLAP: August 2024 data may appear in reports dated September or October 2024 (retrospective sitreps) — do not restrict source search strictly to August publication dates

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Mpox (Monkeypox).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), WHO AFRO situation reports, and Africa CDC bulletins reporting Mpox cases and deaths in DRC for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON and Africa CDC are the highest-priority primary reporting channels for DRC Mpox during the August 2024 outbreak escalation period. These sources contain extractable confirmed, probable, suspected case counts and deaths at national and subnational level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique) and INRB epidemiological bulletins (bulletins épidémiologiques) for Mpox in DRC covering August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The DRC MoH and INRB are the national authoritative sources for subnational (province and health zone) Mpox surveillance data. French-language bulletins are the primary format and are essential for subnational_location and locality field extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Mpox situation reports and multi-country updates covering DRC for the period 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO global Mpox sitreps published in August 2024 aggregate DRC-specific data and may include subnational breakdowns, clade I/Ib distinctions, and weekly case/death counts extractable for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (Global.health, Our World in Data, ProMED) that aggregate DRC Mpox case and death counts for August 2024 for cross-validation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be held back and used to validate extracted records from primary collection sources without leakage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ECDC rapid risk assessments or technical reports covering DRC Mpox clade I/Ib for August 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ECDC published technical assessments on DRC Mpox clade Ib in mid-2024 that include epidemiological summaries usable for validation of case and death counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and preprints describing DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology, case definitions, and surveillance methodology for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources clarify case definitions (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), clade classification, and count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly) needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify news and situation report sources (Reuters, AP, Reliefweb, OCHA) covering DRC Mpox outbreak in August 2024 for early signal detection and subnational location corroboration.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and humanitarian situation reports may contain early outbreak signals, subnational location names, and corroborating counts that support collection and help identify gaps in official reporting.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident), unclear reporting periods, or mixed clade data for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: DRC Mpox reporting in August 2024 involved both clade I and clade Ib, cumulative and weekly counts, and national vs. subnational aggregations. Sources that do not clearly distinguish these dimensions require human adjudication.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: WHO AFRO, WHO HQ Disease Outbreak News, Africa CDC, DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique, Hygiène et Prévention), and INRB (Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale) are the authoritative primary reporting agencies for DRC Mpox. These sources publish weekly and monthly epidemiological bulletins with subnational (province, health zone) case and death breakdowns, confirmed/probable/suspected case classifications, and clade I/Ib distinctions directly relevant to the August 2024...[truncated]

WHO global Mpox situation reports, ECDC rapid risk assessments, OCHA humanitarian situation reports, and Reliefweb updates provide independently compiled DRC Mpox data for August 2024. These serve as validation sources because they aggregate data from official DRC sources but are published independently, enabling cross-check of case and death counts.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints (PubMed, medRxiv, Lancet, NEJM, Eurosurveillance) on DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology published in 2024 provide case definitions, surveillance methodology context, and may contain extractable case/death data for the August 2024 period. Essential for interpreting count semantics and normalizing confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.

Structured public-health databases including Global.health line lists, Our World in Data Mpox tracker, WHO Mpox data repository, and ProMED archive provide machine-readable or structured DRC Mpox counts for August 2024. These are held back for validation to cross-check extracted records from primary collection sources.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC), humanitarian portals (Reliefweb, OCHA), and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Health Policy Watch) published DRC Mpox outbreak coverage in August 2024 coinciding with the WHO PHEIC declaration. These sources provide early outbreak signals, subnational location corroboration, and may cite official figures directly quotable as evidence.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints (PubMed, medRxiv, Lancet, NEJM, Eurosurveillance) on DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology published in 2024 provide case definitions, surveillance methodology context, and may contain extractable case/death data for the August 2024 period. Essential for interpreting count semantics and normalizing confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.

Structured public-health databases including Global.health line lists, Our World in Data Mpox tracker, WHO Mpox data repository, and ProMED archive provide machine-readable or structured DRC Mpox counts for August 2024. These are held back for validation to cross-check extracted records from primary collection sources.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC), humanitarian portals (Reliefweb, OCHA), and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Health Policy Watch) published DRC Mpox outbreak coverage in August 2024 coinciding with the WHO PHEIC declaration. These sources provide early outbreak signals, subnational location corroboration, and may cite official figures directly quotable as evidence.

query_batch.query: WHO mpox situation report Democratic Republic Congo August 2024 cases deaths provinces
query_batch.query_rationale: WHO (HQ and AFRO) is the highest-authority international source for DRC Mpox epidemiological data. During August 2024, WHO declared a PHEIC for Mpox clade Ib, making weekly situation reports and disease outbreak news (DON) the most likely sources of confirmed/probable/suspected case counts, deaths, and province-level breakdowns. Targeting 'situation report' and 'provinces' increases the chance of retrieving subnational data needed for the target fields.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: WHO AFRO or WHO HQ situation report, disease outbreak news, or epidemiological update PDF/webpage with tabular case counts by province and week
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: who.int domain, AFRO regional office authorship, dated situation report with epidemiological week reference

query_batch.query: mpox variole du singe RDC Congo août 2024 cas décès bulletin épidémiologique INRB ministère santé
query_batch.query_rationale: DRC's national surveillance bulletins are published in French by the Ministère de la Santé Publique and INRB (Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale). These are the primary national-authority sources for confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts with subnational (province/zone de santé) breakdowns. 'Août 2024' is the French for August 2024. Using both 'variole du singe' (legacy term) and 'mpox' (current WHO-preferred term) maximises recall across older and newer documents.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: French-language weekly or monthly epidemiological bulletin (bulletin épidémiologique hebdomadaire/mensuel) from INRB or DRC Ministry of Health with province- or health-zone-level case tables
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: inrb.cd or sante.gouv.cd domain, INRB or Ministère de la Santé authorship, dated bulletin with epidemiological week number

outbreak_terms: urgence de santé publique de portée internationale
official_source_terms: Programme National de Lutte contre le Mpox
likely_reporting_agencies: WHO (World Health Organization) — AFRO Regional Office
WHO Headquarters Geneva — Disease Outbreak News (DON)
DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique, Hygiène et Prévention)
MSF (Médecins Sans Frontières / Doctors Without Borders)
ECDC (European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control)
validation_source_categories: DRC Ministry of Health official bulletins
peer-reviewed epidemiological studies (Lancet, NEJM, Eurosurveillance, PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases)
disease_intelligence.suggested_geographic_granularity: ["national (DRC)", "provincial (e.g., South Kivu, North Kivu, Equateur, Sankuru, Maniema, Kinshasa)", "health zone (zone de santé)", "health area (aire de santé)"]
disease_intelligence.suggested_time_granularity: ["weekly (epidemiological week / semaine épidémiologique)", "monthly cumulative", "daily if available from sitreps"]
count_semantics_notes: DRC surveillance distinguishes: cas suspects (suspected), cas probables (probable), cas confirmés (confirmed by PCR/lab) — record each separately
Cumulative case counts are frequently reported; always note whether figure is cumulative-to-date or incident (new cases in period)
CFR (case fatality rate) in DRC clade I outbreaks is historically higher (~3–10%) than global clade IIb — do not apply global CFR benchmarks
Deaths may be underreported relative to cases due to community-level mortality not captured in facility-based surveillance
Hospitalization data is sparse in DRC context; capture when available but expect gaps
Epidemiological week (EW/SE) numbering should be mapped to calendar dates for the August 2024 window (EW31–EW35 approximately)
Some reports aggregate multiple provinces; disaggregate to province level where possible
disambiguation_risks: 'Mpox' vs. 'Smallpox' (variole) — ensure correct disease mapping
Clade I vs. Clade II vs. Clade Ib — DRC 2024 outbreak is predominantly clade I and emerging clade Ib; do not conflate with global clade IIb outbreak
'Monkeypox' legacy term still used in older documents and some French-language sources ('variole du singe') — treat as equivalent
Case classification ambiguity: DRC surveillance often reports 'cas suspects' as the primary count; confirmed PCR cases are a subset — do not sum across categories
Cumulative vs. incident (new) case counts — distinguish clearly; many sitreps report cumulative totals
Health zone vs. province — subnational granularity varies by source; record at finest available level
Pediatric mpox in DRC is disproportionately high — age-stratified data may be available and should be captured separately if present
PHEIC declaration (August 2024) may cause surge in reporting and retrospective revisions — flag data vintage carefully
exclusion_terms: mpox historical pre-2024 unless explicitly comparative
chickenpox (varicelle) — distinct disease, do not conflate
warnings: PHEIC CONTEXT: WHO declared mpox a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on 14 August 2024, driven substantially by the DRC clade Ib outbreak — expect elevated reporting volume, potential data revisions, and multiple overlapping sitreps during this window

CLADE SPECIFICITY: DRC August 2024 data involves both endemic clade I and the newly characterized clade Ib (associated with sexual transmission networks in eastern DRC, particularly South Kivu) — distinguish clade when reported
DATA COMPLETENESS: DRC surveillance infrastructure is resource-constrained; significant underreporting is expected, especially at health-zone and community levels
LANGUAGE: Primary official DRC sources are in French — query terms and source reading must accommodate French-language content ('cas', 'décès', 'flambée', 'bulletin épidémiologique', etc.)
TEMPORAL OVERLAP: August 2024 data may appear in reports dated September or October 2024 (retrospective sitreps) — do not restrict source search strictly to August publication dates

EXTRACTION MODEL WARNING (from task_input_warnings): extraction_record_model_still_hantavirus_named — verify that the extraction schema in use has been updated to Mpox-appropriate field names before ingestion; do not allow Hantavirus-specific fields to contaminate Mpox records

SOURCE DISCOVERY WARNING (from task_input_warnings): source_discovery_not_yet_disease_generic — source discovery pipeline may not yet be fully generalized; manually verify that Mpox-specific source categories (WHO DON, Africa CDC, INRB, DRC MoH) are included in the discovery scope
DOUBLE-COUNTING RISK: WHO, Africa CDC, and DRC MoH may report the same underlying data — cross-reference source chains and avoid double-counting when aggregating
SUBNATIONAL GRANULARITY: Prioritize province-level and health-zone-level data; national aggregates alone are insufficient for this collection task
EVIDENCE QUOTE REQUIREMENT: Every extracted record must include a verbatim evidence_quote from the source document supporting the numeric values recorded

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), WHO AFRO situation reports, and Africa CDC bulletins reporting Mpox cases and deaths in DRC for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON and Africa CDC are the highest-priority primary reporting channels for DRC Mpox during the August 2024 outbreak escalation period. These sources contain extractable confirmed, probable, suspected case counts and deaths at national and subnational level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique) and INRB epidemiological bulletins (bulletins épidémiologiques) for Mpox in DRC covering August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The DRC MoH and INRB are the national authoritative sources for subnational (province and health zone) Mpox surveillance data. French-language bulletins are the primary format and are essential for subnational_location and locality field extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Mpox situation reports and multi-country updates covering DRC for the period 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO global Mpox sitreps published in August 2024 aggregate DRC-specific data and may include subnational breakdowns, clade I/Ib distinctions, and weekly case/death counts extractable for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (Global.health, Our World in Data, ProMED) that aggregate DRC Mpox case and death counts for August 2024 for cross-validation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be held back and used to validate extracted records from primary collection sources without leakage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ECDC rapid risk assessments or technical reports covering DRC Mpox clade I/Ib for August 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ECDC published technical assessments on DRC Mpox clade Ib in mid-2024 that include epidemiological summaries usable for validation of case and death counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and preprints describing DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology, case definitions, and surveillance methodology for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources clarify case definitions (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), clade classification, and count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly) needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify news and situation report sources (Reuters, AP, Reliefweb, OCHA) covering DRC Mpox outbreak in August 2024 for early signal detection and subnational location corroboration.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and humanitarian situation reports may contain early outbreak signals, subnational location names, and corroborating counts that support collection and help identify gaps in official reporting.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident), unclear reporting periods, or mixed clade data for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: DRC Mpox reporting in August 2024 involved both clade I and clade Ib, cumulative and weekly counts, and national vs. subnational aggregations. Sources that do not clearly distinguish these dimensions require human adjudication.

These sources publish weekly and monthly epidemiological bulletins with subnational (province, health zone) case and death breakdowns, confirmed/probable/suspected case classifications, and clade I/Ib distinctions directly relevant to the August 2024...[truncated]

These sources provide early outbreak signals, subnational location corroboration, and may cite official figures directly quotable as evidence.

query_batch.query: WHO mpox situation report Democratic Republic Congo August 2024 cases deaths provinces
query_batch.query_rationale: WHO (HQ and AFRO) is the highest-authority international source for DRC Mpox epidemiological data. During August 2024, WHO declared a PHEIC for Mpox clade Ib, making weekly situation reports and disease outbreak news (DON) the most likely sources of confirmed/probable/suspected case counts, deaths, and province-level breakdowns. Targeting 'situation report' and 'provinces' increases the chance of retrieving subnational data needed for the target fields.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: WHO AFRO or WHO HQ situation report, disease outbreak news, or epidemiological update PDF/webpage with tabular case counts by province and week
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: who.int domain, AFRO regional office authorship, dated situation report with epidemiological week reference

query_batch.query: mpox variole du singe RDC Congo août 2024 cas décès bulletin épidémiologique INRB ministère santé
query_batch.query_rationale: DRC's national surveillance bulletins are published in French by the Ministère de la Santé Publique and INRB (Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale). These are the primary national-authority sources for confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts with subnational (province/zone de santé) breakdowns. 'Août 2024' is the French for August 2024. Using both 'variole du singe' (legacy term) and 'mpox' (current WHO-preferred term) maximises recall across older and newer documents.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: French-language weekly or monthly epidemiological bulletin (bulletin épidémiologique hebdomadaire/mensuel) from INRB or DRC Ministry of Health with province- or health-zone-level case tables
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: inrb.cd or sante.gouv.cd domain, INRB or Ministère de la Santé authorship, dated bulletin with epidemiological week number

'Clade' is included because August 2024 reporting heavily distinguished clade Ib (DRC-origin) from clade IIb, and documents using this terminology are likely to contain granular DRC data.

disease_intelligence.suggested_time_granularity: ["weekly (epidemiological week / semaine épidémiologique)", "monthly cumulative", "daily if available from sitreps"]
count_semantics_notes: DRC surveillance distinguishes: cas suspects (suspected), cas probables (probable), cas confirmés (confirmed by PCR/lab) — record each separately
Cumulative case counts are frequently reported; always note whether figure is cumulative-to-date or incident (new cases in period)
CFR (case fatality rate) in DRC clade I outbreaks is historically higher (~3–10%) than global clade IIb — do not apply global CFR benchmarks
Deaths may be underreported relative to cases due to community-level mortality not captured in facility-based surveillance
Hospitalization data is sparse in DRC context; capture when available but expect gaps
Epidemiological week (EW/SE) numbering should be mapped to calendar dates for the August 2024 window (EW31–EW35 approximately)
Some reports aggregate multiple provinces; disaggregate to province level where possible
disambiguation_risks: 'Mpox' vs. 'Smallpox' (variole) — ensure correct disease mapping
Clade I vs. Clade II vs. Clade Ib — DRC 2024 outbreak is predominantly clade I and emerging clade Ib; do not conflate with global clade IIb outbreak
'Monkeypox' legacy term still used in older documents and some French-language sources ('variole du singe') — treat as equivalent
Case classification ambiguity: DRC surveillance often reports 'cas suspects' as the primary count; confirmed PCR cases are a subset — do not sum across categories
Cumulative vs. incident (new) case counts — distinguish clearly; many sitreps report cumulative totals
Health zone vs. province — subnational granularity varies by source; record at finest available level
Pediatric mpox in DRC is disproportionately high — age-stratified data may be available and should be captured separately if present
PHEIC declaration (August 2024) may cause surge in reporting and retrospective revisions — flag data vintage carefully
exclusion_terms: mpox historical pre-2024 unless explicitly comparative
chickenpox (varicelle) — distinct disease, do not conflate

LANGUAGE: Primary official DRC sources are in French — query terms and source reading must accommodate French-language content ('cas', 'décès', 'flambée', 'bulletin épidémiologique', etc.)

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Mpox (Monkeypox).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), WHO AFRO situation reports, and Africa CDC bulletins reporting Mpox cases and deaths in DRC for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON and Africa CDC are the highest-priority primary reporting channels for DRC Mpox during the August 2024 outbreak escalation period. These sources contain extractable confirmed, probable, suspected case counts and deaths at national and subnational level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique) and INRB epidemiological bulletins (bulletins épidémiologiques) for Mpox in DRC covering August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The DRC MoH and INRB are the national authoritative sources for subnational (province and health zone) Mpox surveillance data. French-language bulletins are the primary format and are essential for subnational_location and locality field extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Mpox situation reports and multi-country updates covering DRC for the period 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO global Mpox sitreps published in August 2024 aggregate DRC-specific data and may include subnational breakdowns, clade I/Ib distinctions, and weekly case/death counts extractable for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (Global.health, Our World in Data, ProMED) that aggregate DRC Mpox case and death counts for August 2024 for cross-validation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be held back and used to validate extracted records from primary collection sources without leakage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ECDC rapid risk assessments or technical reports covering DRC Mpox clade I/Ib for August 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ECDC published technical assessments on DRC Mpox clade Ib in mid-2024 that include epidemiological summaries usable for validation of case and death counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and preprints describing DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology, case definitions, and surveillance methodology for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources clarify case definitions (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), clade classification, and count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly) needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify news and situation report sources (Reuters, AP, Reliefweb, OCHA) covering DRC Mpox outbreak in August 2024 for early signal detection and subnational location corroboration.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and humanitarian situation reports may contain early outbreak signals, subnational location names, and corroborating counts that support collection and help identify gaps in official reporting.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident), unclear reporting periods, or mixed clade data for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: DRC Mpox reporting in August 2024 involved both clade I and clade Ib, cumulative and weekly counts, and national vs. subnational aggregations. Sources that do not clearly distinguish these dimensions require human adjudication.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: WHO AFRO, WHO HQ Disease Outbreak News, Africa CDC, DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique, Hygiène et Prévention), and INRB (Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale) are the authoritative primary reporting agencies for DRC Mpox. These sources publish weekly and monthly epidemiological bulletins with subnational (province, health zone) case and death breakdowns, confirmed/probable/suspected case classifications, and clade I/Ib distinctions directly relevant to the August 2024...[truncated]

WHO global Mpox situation reports, ECDC rapid risk assessments, OCHA humanitarian situation reports, and Reliefweb updates provide independently compiled DRC Mpox data for August 2024. These serve as validation sources because they aggregate data from official DRC sources but are published independently, enabling cross-check of case and death counts.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints (PubMed, medRxiv, Lancet, NEJM, Eurosurveillance) on DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology published in 2024 provide case definitions, surveillance methodology context, and may contain extractable case/death data for the August 2024 period. Essential for interpreting count semantics and normalizing confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.

Structured public-health databases including Global.health line lists, Our World in Data Mpox tracker, WHO Mpox data repository, and ProMED archive provide machine-readable or structured DRC Mpox counts for August 2024. These are held back for validation to cross-check extracted records from primary collection sources.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC), humanitarian portals (Reliefweb, OCHA), and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Health Policy Watch) published DRC Mpox outbreak coverage in August 2024 coinciding with the WHO PHEIC declaration. These sources provide early outbreak signals, subnational location corroboration, and may cite official figures directly quotable as evidence.

query_batch.query: WHO mpox situation report Democratic Republic Congo August 2024 cases deaths provinces
query_batch.query_rationale: WHO (HQ and AFRO) is the highest-authority international source for DRC Mpox epidemiological data. During August 2024, WHO declared a PHEIC for Mpox clade Ib, making weekly situation reports and disease outbreak news (DON) the most likely sources of confirmed/probable/suspected case counts, deaths, and province-level breakdowns. Targeting 'situation report' and 'provinces' increases the chance of retrieving subnational data needed for the target fields.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: WHO AFRO or WHO HQ situation report, disease outbreak news, or epidemiological update PDF/webpage with tabular case counts by province and week
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: who.int domain, AFRO regional office authorship, dated situation report with epidemiological week reference

query_batch.query: mpox variole du singe RDC Congo août 2024 cas décès bulletin épidémiologique INRB ministère santé
query_batch.query_rationale: DRC's national surveillance bulletins are published in French by the Ministère de la Santé Publique and INRB (Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale). These are the primary national-authority sources for confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts with subnational (province/zone de santé) breakdowns. 'Août 2024' is the French for August 2024. Using both 'variole du singe' (legacy term) and 'mpox' (current WHO-preferred term) maximises recall across older and newer documents.

iterative_search_queries.query: WHO mpox situation report Democratic Republic Congo August 2024 cases deaths provinces
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: WHO (HQ and AFRO) is the highest-authority international source for DRC Mpox epidemiological data. During August 2024, WHO declared a PHEIC for Mpox clade Ib, making weekly situation reports and disease outbreak news (DON) the most likely sources of confirmed/probable/suspected case counts, deaths, and province-level breakdowns. Targeting 'situation report' and 'provinces' increases the chance of retrieving subnational data needed for the target fields.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: WHO AFRO or WHO HQ situation report, disease outbreak news, or epidemiological update PDF/webpage with tabular case counts by province and week
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: who.int domain, AFRO regional office authorship, dated situation report with epidemiological week reference

iterative_search_queries.query: mpox variole du singe RDC Congo août 2024 cas décès bulletin épidémiologique INRB ministère santé
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: DRC's national surveillance bulletins are published in French by the Ministère de la Santé Publique and INRB (Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale). These are the primary national-authority sources for confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts with subnational (province/zone de santé) breakdowns. 'Août 2024' is the French for August 2024. Using both 'variole du singe' (legacy term) and 'mpox' (current WHO-preferred term) maximises recall across older and newer documents.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: French-language weekly or monthly epidemiological bulletin (bulletin épidémiologique hebdomadaire/mensuel) from INRB or DRC Ministry of Health with province- or health-zone-level case tables

iterative_search_queries.query: mpox outbreak DRC Congo August 2024 cases deaths clade WHO AFRO epidemiological update weekly
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Broadens the WHO/AFRO query to capture epidemiological updates, clade-specific reporting (clade I, clade Ib), and any CDC or Africa CDC situation reports published during August 2024. The term 'weekly' targets periodic surveillance summaries most likely to contain the date-windowed case counts needed. 'Clade' is included because August 2024 reporting heavily distinguished clade Ib (DRC-origin) from clade IIb, and documents using this terminology are likely to contain granular DRC data.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: WHO AFRO, Africa CDC, or US CDC situation report or epidemiological update with weekly case counts for DRC, ideally with province-level tables
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: afro.who.int, africacdc.org, or cdc.gov domain; dated weekly epidemiological update; explicit case count tables

count_semantics_notes: DRC surveillance distinguishes: cas suspects (suspected), cas probables (probable), cas confirmés (confirmed by PCR/lab) — record each separately
Cumulative case counts are frequently reported; always note whether figure is cumulative-to-date or incident (new cases in period)
CFR (case fatality rate) in DRC clade I outbreaks is historically higher (~3–10%) than global clade IIb — do not apply global CFR benchmarks
Deaths may be underreported relative to cases due to community-level mortality not captured in facility-based surveillance
Hospitalization data is sparse in DRC context; capture when available but expect gaps
Epidemiological week (EW/SE) numbering should be mapped to calendar dates for the August 2024 window (EW31–EW35 approximately)
Some reports aggregate multiple provinces; disaggregate to province level where possible
disambiguation_risks: 'Mpox' vs. 'Smallpox' (variole) — ensure correct disease mapping
Clade I vs. Clade II vs. Clade Ib — DRC 2024 outbreak is predominantly clade I and emerging clade Ib; do not conflate with global clade IIb outbreak
'Monkeypox' legacy term still used in older documents and some French-language sources ('variole du singe') — treat as equivalent
Case classification ambiguity: DRC surveillance often reports 'cas suspects' as the primary count; confirmed PCR cases are a subset — do not sum across categories
Cumulative vs. incident (new) case counts — distinguish clearly; many sitreps report cumulative totals
Health zone vs. province — subnational granularity varies by source; record at finest available level
Pediatric mpox in DRC is disproportionately high — age-stratified data may be available and should be captured separately if present
PHEIC declaration (August 2024) may cause surge in reporting and retrospective revisions — flag data vintage carefully
exclusion_terms: mpox historical pre-2024 unless explicitly comparative
chickenpox (varicelle) — distinct disease, do not conflate

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), WHO AFRO situation reports, and Africa CDC bulletins reporting Mpox cases and deaths in DRC for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON and Africa CDC are the highest-priority primary reporting channels for DRC Mpox during the August 2024 outbreak escalation period. These sources contain extractable confirmed, probable, suspected case counts and deaths at national and subnational level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique) and INRB epidemiological bulletins (bulletins épidémiologiques) for Mpox in DRC covering August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The DRC MoH and INRB are the national authoritative sources for subnational (province and health zone) Mpox surveillance data. French-language bulletins are the primary format and are essential for subnational_location and locality field extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Mpox situation reports and multi-country updates covering DRC for the period 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO global Mpox sitreps published in August 2024 aggregate DRC-specific data and may include subnational breakdowns, clade I/Ib distinctions, and weekly case/death counts extractable for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (Global.health, Our World in Data, ProMED) that aggregate DRC Mpox case and death counts for August 2024 for cross-validation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be held back and used to validate extracted records from primary collection sources without leakage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ECDC rapid risk assessments or technical reports covering DRC Mpox clade I/Ib for August 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ECDC published technical assessments on DRC Mpox clade Ib in mid-2024 that include epidemiological summaries usable for validation of case and death counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and preprints describing DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology, case definitions, and surveillance methodology for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources clarify case definitions (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), clade classification, and count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly) needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify news and situation report sources (Reuters, AP, Reliefweb, OCHA) covering DRC Mpox outbreak in August 2024 for early signal detection and subnational location corroboration.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and humanitarian situation reports may contain early outbreak signals, subnational location names, and corroborating counts that support collection and help identify gaps in official reporting.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident), unclear reporting periods, or mixed clade data for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: DRC Mpox reporting in August 2024 involved both clade I and clade Ib, cumulative and weekly counts, and national vs. subnational aggregations. Sources that do not clearly distinguish these dimensions require human adjudication.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: WHO AFRO, WHO HQ Disease Outbreak News, Africa CDC, DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique, Hygiène et Prévention), and INRB (Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale) are the authoritative primary reporting agencies for DRC Mpox. These sources publish weekly and monthly epidemiological bulletins with subnational (province, health zone) case and death breakdowns, confirmed/probable/suspected case classifications, and clade I/Ib distinctions directly relevant to the August 2024...[truncated]

WHO global Mpox situation reports, ECDC rapid risk assessments, OCHA humanitarian situation reports, and Reliefweb updates provide independently compiled DRC Mpox data for August 2024. These serve as validation sources because they aggregate data from official DRC sources but are published independently, enabling cross-check of case and death counts.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints (PubMed, medRxiv, Lancet, NEJM, Eurosurveillance) on DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology published in 2024 provide case definitions, surveillance methodology context, and may contain extractable case/death data for the August 2024 period. Essential for interpreting count semantics and normalizing confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.

Structured public-health databases including Global.health line lists, Our World in Data Mpox tracker, WHO Mpox data repository, and ProMED archive provide machine-readable or structured DRC Mpox counts for August 2024. These are held back for validation to cross-check extracted records from primary collection sources.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC), humanitarian portals (Reliefweb, OCHA), and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Health Policy Watch) published DRC Mpox outbreak coverage in August 2024 coinciding with the WHO PHEIC declaration. These sources provide early outbreak signals, subnational location corroboration, and may cite official figures directly quotable as evidence.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), WHO AFRO situation reports, and Africa CDC bulletins reporting Mpox cases and deaths in DRC for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON and Africa CDC are the highest-priority primary reporting channels for DRC Mpox during the August 2024 outbreak escalation period. These sources contain extractable confirmed, probable, suspected case counts and deaths at national and subnational level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique) and INRB epidemiological bulletins (bulletins épidémiologiques) for Mpox in DRC covering August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The DRC MoH and INRB are the national authoritative sources for subnational (province and health zone) Mpox surveillance data. French-language bulletins are the primary format and are essential for subnational_location and locality field extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Mpox situation reports and multi-country updates covering DRC for the period 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO global Mpox sitreps published in August 2024 aggregate DRC-specific data and may include subnational breakdowns, clade I/Ib distinctions, and weekly case/death counts extractable for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (Global.health, Our World in Data, ProMED) that aggregate DRC Mpox case and death counts for August 2024 for cross-validation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be held back and used to validate extracted records from primary collection sources without leakage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ECDC rapid risk assessments or technical reports covering DRC Mpox clade I/Ib for August 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ECDC published technical assessments on DRC Mpox clade Ib in mid-2024 that include epidemiological summaries usable for validation of case and death counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and preprints describing DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology, case definitions, and surveillance methodology for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources clarify case definitions (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), clade classification, and count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly) needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify news and situation report sources (Reuters, AP, Reliefweb, OCHA) covering DRC Mpox outbreak in August 2024 for early signal detection and subnational location corroboration.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and humanitarian situation reports may contain early outbreak signals, subnational location names, and corroborating counts that support collection and help identify gaps in official reporting.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident), unclear reporting periods, or mixed clade data for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: DRC Mpox reporting in August 2024 involved both clade I and clade Ib, cumulative and weekly counts, and national vs. subnational aggregations. Sources that do not clearly distinguish these dimensions require human adjudication.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: WHO AFRO, WHO HQ Disease Outbreak News, Africa CDC, DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique, Hygiène et Prévention), and INRB (Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale) are the authoritative primary reporting agencies for DRC Mpox. These sources publish weekly and monthly epidemiological bulletins with subnational (province, health zone) case and death breakdowns, confirmed/probable/suspected case classifications, and clade I/Ib distinctions directly relevant to the August 2024...[truncated]

WHO global Mpox situation reports, ECDC rapid risk assessments, OCHA humanitarian situation reports, and Reliefweb updates provide independently compiled DRC Mpox data for August 2024. These serve as validation sources because they aggregate data from official DRC sources but are published independently, enabling cross-check of case and death counts.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints (PubMed, medRxiv, Lancet, NEJM, Eurosurveillance) on DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology published in 2024 provide case definitions, surveillance methodology context, and may contain extractable case/death data for the August 2024 period. Essential for interpreting count semantics and normalizing confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.

Structured public-health databases including Global.health line lists, Our World in Data Mpox tracker, WHO Mpox data repository, and ProMED archive provide machine-readable or structured DRC Mpox counts for August 2024. These are held back for validation to cross-check extracted records from primary collection sources.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC), humanitarian portals (Reliefweb, OCHA), and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Health Policy Watch) published DRC Mpox outbreak coverage in August 2024 coinciding with the WHO PHEIC declaration. These sources provide early outbreak signals, subnational location corroboration, and may cite official figures directly quotable as evidence.

query_batch.query: WHO mpox situation report Democratic Republic Congo August 2024 cases deaths provinces
query_batch.query_rationale: WHO (HQ and AFRO) is the highest-authority international source for DRC Mpox epidemiological data. During August 2024, WHO declared a PHEIC for Mpox clade Ib, making weekly situation reports and disease outbreak news (DON) the most likely sources of confirmed/probable/suspected case counts, deaths, and province-level breakdowns. Targeting 'situation report' and 'provinces' increases the chance of retrieving subnational data needed for the target fields.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: WHO AFRO or WHO HQ situation report, disease outbreak news, or epidemiological update PDF/webpage with tabular case counts by province and week
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: who.int domain, AFRO regional office authorship, dated situation report with epidemiological week reference

query_batch.query: mpox variole du singe RDC Congo août 2024 cas décès bulletin épidémiologique INRB ministère santé

Using both 'variole du singe' (legacy term) and 'mpox' (current WHO-preferred term) maximises recall across older and newer documents.

disambiguation_risks: 'Mpox' vs. 'Smallpox' (variole) — ensure correct disease mapping

'Monkeypox' legacy term still used in older documents and some French-language sources ('variole du singe') — treat as equivalent
Case classification ambiguity: DRC surveillance often reports 'cas suspects' as the primary count; confirmed PCR cases are a subset — do not sum across categories
Cumulative vs. incident (new) case counts — distinguish clearly; many sitreps report cumulative totals
Health zone vs. province — subnational granularity varies by source; record at finest available level
Pediatric mpox in DRC is disproportionately high — age-stratified data may be available and should be captured separately if present
PHEIC declaration (August 2024) may cause surge in reporting and retrospective revisions — flag data vintage carefully

query_batch.query: WHO mpox situation report Democratic Republic Congo August 2024 cases deaths provinces
query_batch.query_rationale: WHO (HQ and AFRO) is the highest-authority international source for DRC Mpox epidemiological data. During August 2024, WHO declared a PHEIC for Mpox clade Ib, making weekly situation reports and disease outbreak news (DON) the most likely sources of confirmed/probable/suspected case counts, deaths, and province-level breakdowns. Targeting 'situation report' and 'provinces' increases the chance of retrieving subnational data needed for the target fields.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: WHO AFRO or WHO HQ situation report, disease outbreak news, or epidemiological update PDF/webpage with tabular case counts by province and week
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: who.int domain, AFRO regional office authorship, dated situation report with epidemiological week reference

query_batch.query: mpox variole du singe RDC Congo août 2024 cas décès bulletin épidémiologique INRB ministère santé
query_batch.query_rationale: DRC's national surveillance bulletins are published in French by the Ministère de la Santé Publique and INRB (Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale). These are the primary national-authority sources for confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts with subnational (province/zone de santé) breakdowns. 'Août 2024' is the French for August 2024. Using both 'variole du singe' (legacy term) and 'mpox' (current WHO-preferred term) maximises recall across older and newer documents.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: French-language weekly or monthly epidemiological bulletin (bulletin épidémiologique hebdomadaire/mensuel) from INRB or DRC Ministry of Health with province- or health-zone-level case tables

iterative_search_queries.query: WHO mpox situation report Democratic Republic Congo August 2024 cases deaths provinces
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: WHO (HQ and AFRO) is the highest-authority international source for DRC Mpox epidemiological data. During August 2024, WHO declared a PHEIC for Mpox clade Ib, making weekly situation reports and disease outbreak news (DON) the most likely sources of confirmed/probable/suspected case counts, deaths, and province-level breakdowns. Targeting 'situation report' and 'provinces' increases the chance of retrieving subnational data needed for the target fields.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: WHO AFRO or WHO HQ situation report, disease outbreak news, or epidemiological update PDF/webpage with tabular case counts by province and week
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: who.int domain, AFRO regional office authorship, dated situation report with epidemiological week reference

iterative_search_queries.query: mpox variole du singe RDC Congo août 2024 cas décès bulletin épidémiologique INRB ministère santé
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: DRC's national surveillance bulletins are published in French by the Ministère de la Santé Publique and INRB (Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale). These are the primary national-authority sources for confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts with subnational (province/zone de santé) breakdowns. 'Août 2024' is the French for August 2024. Using both 'variole du singe' (legacy term) and 'mpox' (current WHO-preferred term) maximises recall across older and newer documents.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: French-language weekly or monthly epidemiological bulletin (bulletin épidémiologique hebdomadaire/mensuel) from INRB or DRC Ministry of Health with province- or health-zone-level case tables
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: inrb.cd or sante.gouv.cd domain, INRB or Ministère de la Santé authorship, dated bulletin with epidemiological week number

iterative_search_queries.query: mpox outbreak DRC Congo August 2024 cases deaths clade WHO AFRO epidemiological update weekly
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Broadens the WHO/AFRO query to capture epidemiological updates, clade-specific reporting (clade I, clade Ib), and any CDC or Africa CDC situation reports published during August 2024. The term 'weekly' targets periodic surveillance summaries most likely to contain the date-windowed case counts needed. 'Clade' is included because August 2024 reporting heavily distinguished clade Ib (DRC-origin) from clade IIb, and documents using this terminology are likely to contain granular DRC data.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: WHO AFRO, Africa CDC, or US CDC situation report or epidemiological update with weekly case counts for DRC, ideally with province-level tables
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: afro.who.int, africacdc.org, or cdc.gov domain; dated weekly epidemiological update; explicit case count tables

Combining it with direct WHO, Africa CDC, and ECDC domain restrictions in a single query maximises the chance of surfacing situation reports, flash updates, and epidemiological bulletins that contain August 2024 DRC Mpox data with subnational granularity.
